summary: Thurston County, WA wooden lookout from the 1930s, abandoned in 1958 and now gone; four concrete footings reported on the summit inside a private timber tract.

facts.status_note: The tower is gone. A trip report describes four concrete footings on the summit.

access.note: Private Weyerhaeuser Vail Tree Farm land behind gates; no entry August 1 to December 31 without a special access permit; owner asks hikers to come only when the gate is closed and no harvest is under way

visit.trail_note: No tower remains. The trip report says the owner asks hikers to come only when the gate is closed and no harvest is under way

facts.agency: Washington State Division of Forestry (Department of Natural Resources)

events.note: Both lookout listings give only the 1930s; 1930 is the year on the record (see corrections)
Abandoned in 1958 per the register, firelookout.com and the trip report
Registered April 6, 2020 on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register

corrections.why: The Former Fire Lookout Sites register and firelookout.com both give the 1930s as the build decade, not a single year

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The lookout listings name the state Division of Forestry (one pairs it with DNR); the trip report names Weyerhaeuser as the landowner today, so the two describe the agency and the current owner

sources.title: Miller Hill Lookout Site - Weyerhaeuser Vail Tree Farm

notes_for_editor: Gone lookout. The four footings come from one undated trip report, so treat them as the last described state. Both listings give only the 1930s for the build, so the record's 1930 is kept as the event year with a note and a correction. Access is restricted: private Weyerhaeuser timber land with gate rules. The story says so plainly and does not encourage a visit. No staffing, fire or rental information in the sources read, so none in the story. Used 1 WebSearch and 5 page reads.
